sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India, Guwahati Circle: Ambari archaeological site
sources.note: Direct excavation summary. Earlier medieval occupation circa seventh to twelfth centuries; Chinese celadon tenth to twelfth centuries. Earliest tank and hearth claims are not assigned to the medieval phase. Geometry is independently decoded from repository snapshots.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India: Rock inscription on the bank of the Brahmaputra, Tezpur
sources.note: Direct official description: Harjjaravarman, Gupta year 510 = 829 to 830 CE; royal fishing boundary warning. This later evidence contextualizes the northeast polygon, which disappears from this label after 800.

sources.title: Indian Journal of History of Science (2022): Fishing, migration, and settlement: a study of Kaibartas in Majuli Island, Assam
sources.note: Direct scholarly article, section 7.1 only for Tezpur inscription and state boat service. Present-day Majuli fishing equipment and community practices are not projected backward.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India, Jaipur Circle: Chand Baori
sources.note: Direct fetch failed; complete indexed original description checked. ASI eighth-century attribution differs from Rajasthan Tourism ninth century; public copy retains approximate eighth to ninth centuries. Modern visitor toilet listing is not historical evidence.

sources.title: Rajasthan Tourism: Chand Baori, Abhaneri
sources.note: Direct official account: water conservation, respite from heat and community gathering. Present pavilion not assigned wholesale to earliest building campaign; no measured temperature claim.

sources.title: C. Sivaramamurti: Early Eastern Chalukya Sculpture, Madras Government Museum Bulletin VII.2 (1957; reprint 2000)
sources.note: Direct institutional monograph. Printed pages 1 to 8 for separate Eastern Chalukya history; page 5 for feeding houses, water stations and tanks attributed to Vijayaditya II; page 9 for Chola-supported restoration around 1000. Panegyric battle totals and ethnic language not adopted. Whole monograph counted together.

sources.title: Government Museum Chennai: Catalogue of Copper Plate Grants
sources.note: Direct museum catalogue, Eastern Chalukyas entries 10, 15 and 17. Reign dating of Amma I approximately 918 to 925, not exact issue date for Cevuru; Amma II Jain donation in entry 17 on printed page 8 / human PDF page 18. Whole catalogue counted as one work.

sources.title: Dániel Balogh, DHARMA: Cevuru plates of Amma I
sources.note: Direct digital critical edition collated against B. Ch. Chhabra, Epigraphia Indica XXVII, pages 41 to 47, original and rubbings. English and French translations checked. First rice-feeding gloss explicitly in French note 13. Sanskrit svasti and Telugu koḍu are secure readings; normalized modern Devanagari only for Sanskrit, Roman scholarly transcription for Telugu.

sources.title: Dániel Balogh, DHARMA: Varppongu grant of Vijayaditya II
sources.note: Direct critical edition and translation, lines 12 to 19; Piṣṭapura district, lunar eclipse gift, three generations and Vedic learning. Grandson’s damaged personal name omitted rather than silently restoring certainty. Modern edition collates N. Venkataramanayya 1974 and ASI estampages.

sources.title: Dániel Balogh, DHARMA: Ederu plates of Amma I
sources.note: Direct critical edition and translation. Lines 27 to 44 for warfare and Bhima I patronage; lines 53 to 60 for Gonturu and twelve hamlets. Court praise identified as such. Same historical charter as Hultzsch SII I no. 37; repository mirrors and original edition grouped in cumulative budget scan.

sources.title: Indian Museum, Kolkata: Copper plate inscription, accession 11358
sources.note: Direct museum object entry: three copper plates and ring/seal of Vijayaditya II from Chandavallu, Guntur; catalog date broad seventh to ninth centuries. No invented precise excavation circumstances.

proposedOverrides.name: Hindu states
proposedOverrides.summary: A changing regional atlas label, illustrated through distinct medieval communities and kingdoms.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Distinct regional-context card, no aliases. Existing hindu-kingdoms, hindu-kingdoms-1100/rajput-kingdoms and specific dynasties remain separate.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: 700 northeast Bengal/Assam; 800 disconnected northwest/central and eastern peninsular polygons; 900 tiny northern Uttar Pradesh fragment. All principal regional examples therefore require explicit locations and chronology rather than one continuous polity.
batchIdentityNotes.publicCaveats: Overview and first passage expose label jump; Abhaneri outside sampled outlines; Tezpur 829 to 830 later than northeast outline; Vengi tenth-century examples continue after its polygon disappears; Ambari celadon tenth to twelfth century crosses endpoint.
batchIdentityNotes.evidenceLimits: No universal household layout, school enrollment, medical treatment or toilets inferred. Royal charity is not a hospital. Contemporary local language appears through epigraphic transcription, not invented dialogue.
